paragraphs.text: And seeing the multitudes, he went up into the mountain: and when he had sat down, his disciples came unto him:
paragraphs.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ τοὺς ὄχλους ἀνέβη εἰς τὸ ὄρος· καὶ καθίσαντος αὐτοῦ προσῆλθαν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: Idōn de tous ochlous anebē eis to oros· kai kathisantos autou prosēlthan autō hoi mathētai autou·

paragraphs.text: and he opened his mouth and taught them, saying,
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀνοίξας τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς λέγων·
paragraphs.translit: kai anoixas to stoma autou edidasken autous legōn·

paragraphs.text: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
paragraphs.original: Μακάριοι οἱ πτωχοὶ τῷ πνεύματι, ὅτι αὐτῶν ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Makarioi hoi ptōchoi tō pneumati, hoti autōn estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.
paragraphs.original: μακάριοι οἱ πενθοῦντες, ὅτι αὐτοὶ παρακληθήσονται.
paragraphs.translit: makarioi hoi penthountes, hoti autoi paraklēthēsontai.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth.
paragraphs.original: μακάριοι οἱ πραεῖς, ὅτι αὐτοὶ κληρονομήσουσι τὴν γῆν.
paragraphs.translit: makarioi hoi praeis, hoti autoi klēronomēsousi tēn gēn.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled.
paragraphs.original: μακάριοι οἱ πεινῶντες καὶ διψῶντες τὴν δικαιοσύνην, ὅτι αὐτοὶ χορτασθήσονται.
paragraphs.translit: makarioi hoi peinōntes kai dipsōntes tēn dikaiosynēn, hoti autoi chortasthēsontai.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.
paragraphs.original: μακάριοι οἱ ἐλεήμονες, ὅτι αὐτοὶ ἐλεηθήσονται.
paragraphs.translit: makarioi hoi eleēmones, hoti autoi eleēthēsontai.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God.
paragraphs.original: μακάριοι οἱ καθαροὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ, ὅτι αὐτοὶ τὸν θεὸν ὄψονται.
paragraphs.translit: makarioi hoi katharoi tē kardia, hoti autoi ton theon opsontai.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called sons of God.
paragraphs.original: μακάριοι οἱ εἰρηνοποιοί, ὅτι αὐτοὶ υἱοὶ θεοῦ κληθήσονται.
paragraphs.translit: makarioi hoi eirēnopoioi, hoti autoi hyioi theou klēthēsontai.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are they that have been persecuted for righteousness` sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
paragraphs.original: μακάριοι οἱ δεδιωγμένοι ἕνεκεν δικαιοσύνης, ὅτι αὐτῶν ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
paragraphs.translit: makarioi hoi dediōgmenoi heneken dikaiosynēs, hoti autōn estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are ye when [men] shall reproach you, and persecute you, and say all manner of evil against you falsely, for my sake.
paragraphs.original: μακάριοί ἐστε ὅταν ὀνειδίσωσιν ὑμᾶς καὶ διώξωσιν καὶ εἴπωσιν πᾶν πονηρὸν καθʼ ὑμῶν ψευδόμενοι ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: makarioi este hotan oneidisōsin hymas kai diōxōsin kai eipōsin pan ponēron kathʼ hymōn pseudomenoi heneken emou.

paragraphs.text: Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven: for so persecuted they the prophets that were before you.
paragraphs.original: χαίρετε καὶ ἀγαλλιᾶσθε, ὅτι ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν πολὺς ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς· οὕτως γὰρ ἐδίωξαν τοὺς προφήτας τοὺς πρὸ ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: chairete kai agalliasthe, hoti ho misthos hymōn polys en tois ouranois· houtōs gar ediōxan tous prophētas tous pro hymōn.

paragraphs.text: Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost its savor, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out and trodden under foot of men.
paragraphs.original: Ὑμεῖς ἐστε τὸ ἅλας τῆς γῆς· ἐὰν δὲ τὸ ἅλας μωρανθῇ, ἐν τίνι ἁλισθήσεται; εἰς οὐδὲν ἰσχύει ἔτι εἰ μὴ βληθὲν ἔξω καταπατεῖσθαι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων.
paragraphs.translit: Hymeis este to halas tēs gēs· ean de to halas mōranthē, en tini halisthēsetai; eis ouden ischyei eti ei mē blēthen exō katapateisthai hypo tōn anthrōpōn.

paragraphs.text: Ye are the light of the world. A city set on a hill cannot be hid.
paragraphs.original: Ὑμεῖς ἐστε τὸ φῶς τοῦ κόσμου. οὐ δύναται πόλις κρυβῆναι ἐπάνω ὄρους κειμένη·
paragraphs.translit: Hymeis este to phōs tou kosmou. ou dynatai polis krybēnai epanō orous keimenē·

paragraphs.text: Neither do [men] light a lamp, and put it under the bushel, but on the stand; and it shineth unto all that are in the house.
paragraphs.original: οὐδὲ καίουσιν λύχνον καὶ τιθέασιν αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον ἀλλʼ ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν, καὶ λάμπει πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ.
paragraphs.translit: oude kaiousin lychnon kai titheasin auton hypo ton modion allʼ epi tēn lychnian, kai lampei pasin tois en tē oikia.

paragraphs.text: Even so let your light shine before men; that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
paragraphs.original: οὕτως λαμψάτω τὸ φῶς ὑμῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὅπως ἴδωσιν ὑμῶν τὰ καλὰ ἔργα καὶ δοξάσωσιν τὸν πατέρα ὑμῶν τὸν ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: houtōs lampsatō to phōs hymōn emprosthen tōn anthrōpōn, hopōs idōsin hymōn ta kala erga kai doxasōsin ton patera hymōn ton en tois ouranois.

paragraphs.text: Think not that I came to destroy the law or the prophets: I came not to destroy, but to fulfil.
paragraphs.original: Μὴ νομίσητε ὅτι ἦλθον καταλῦσαι τὸν νόμον ἢ τοὺς προφήτας· οὐκ ἦλθον καταλῦσαι ἀλλὰ πληρῶσαι·
paragraphs.translit: Mē nomisēte hoti ēlthon katalysai ton nomon ē tous prophētas· ouk ēlthon katalysai alla plērōsai·

paragraphs.text: For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass away, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass away from the law, till all things be accomplished.
paragraphs.original: ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἕως ἂν παρέλθῃ ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ, ἰῶτα ἓν ἢ μία κεραία οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου, ἕως ἂν πάντα γένηται.
paragraphs.translit: amēn gar legō hymin, heōs an parelthē ho ouranos kai hē gē, iōta hen ē mia keraia ou mē parelthē apo tou nomou, heōs an panta genētai.

paragraphs.text: Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, shall be called least in the kingdom of heaven: but whosoever shall do and teach them, he shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
paragraphs.original: ὃς ἐὰν οὖν λύσῃ μίαν τῶν ἐντολῶν τούτων τῶν ἐλαχίστων καὶ διδάξῃ οὕτως τοὺς ἀνθρώπους, ἐλάχιστος κληθήσεται ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν· ὃς δʼ ἂν ποιήσῃ καὶ διδάξῃ, οὗτος μέγας κληθήσεται ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν.
paragraphs.translit: hos ean oun lysē mian tōn entolōn toutōn tōn elachistōn kai didaxē houtōs tous anthrōpous, elachistos klēthēsetai en tē basileia tōn ouranōn· hos dʼ an poiēsē kai didaxē, houtos megas klēthēsetai en tē basileia tōn ouranōn.

paragraphs.text: For I say unto you, that except your righteousness shall exceed [the righteousness] of the scribes and Pharisees, ye shall in no wise enter into the kingdom of heaven.
paragraphs.original: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐὰν μὴ περισσεύσῃ ὑμῶν ἡ δικαιοσύνη πλεῖον τῶν γραμματέων καὶ Φαρισαίων, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν.
paragraphs.translit: legō gar hymin hoti ean mē perisseusē hymōn hē dikaiosynē pleion tōn grammateōn kai Pharisaiōn, ou mē eiselthēte eis tēn basileian tōn ouranōn.

paragraphs.text: Ye have heard that it was said to them of old time, Thou shalt not kill; and whosoever shall kill shall be in danger of the judgment:
paragraphs.original: Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη τοῖς ἀρχαίοις· Οὐ φονεύσεις· ὃς δʼ ἂν φονεύσῃ, ἔνοχος ἔσται τῇ κρίσει.
paragraphs.translit: Ēkousate hoti errethē tois archaiois· Ou phoneuseis· hos dʼ an phoneusē, enochos estai tē krisei.

paragraphs.text: but I say unto you, that every one who is angry with his brother shall be in danger of the judgment; and whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council; and whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of the hell of fire.
paragraphs.original: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ὀργιζόμενος τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ ἔνοχος ἔσται τῇ κρίσει· ὃς δʼ ἂν εἴπῃ τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ· Ῥακά, ἔνοχος ἔσται τῷ συνεδρίῳ· ὃς δʼ ἂν εἴπῃ· Μωρέ, ἔνοχος ἔσται εἰς τὴν γέενναν τοῦ πυρός.
paragraphs.translit: egō de legō hymin hoti pas ho orgizomenos tō adelphō autou enochos estai tē krisei· hos dʼ an eipē tō adelphō autou· Rhaka, enochos estai tō synedriō· hos dʼ an eipē· Mōre, enochos estai eis tēn geennan tou pyros.

paragraphs.text: If therefore thou art offering thy gift at the altar, and there rememberest that thy brother hath aught against thee,
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν οὖν προσφέρῃς τὸ δῶρόν σου ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον κἀκεῖ μνησθῇς ὅτι ὁ ἀδελφός σου ἔχει τι κατὰ σοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: ean oun prospherēs to dōron sou epi to thysiastērion kakei mnēsthēs hoti ho adelphos sou echei ti kata sou,

paragraphs.text: leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way, first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift.
paragraphs.original: ἄφες ἐκεῖ τὸ δῶρόν σου ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου καὶ ὕπαγε πρῶτον διαλλάγηθι τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου, καὶ τότε ἐλθὼν πρόσφερε τὸ δῶρόν σου.
paragraphs.translit: aphes ekei to dōron sou emprosthen tou thysiastēriou kai hypage prōton diallagēthi tō adelphō sou, kai tote elthōn prosphere to dōron sou.

paragraphs.text: Agree with thine adversary quickly, while thou art with him in the way; lest haply the adversary deliver thee to the judge, and the judge deliver thee to the officer, and thou be cast into prison.
paragraphs.original: ἴσθι εὐνοῶν τῷ ἀντιδίκῳ σου ταχὺ ἕως ὅτου εἶ μετʼ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ, μήποτέ σε παραδῷ ὁ ἀντίδικος τῷ κριτῇ, καὶ ὁ κριτὴς τῷ ὑπηρέτῃ, καὶ εἰς φυλακὴν βληθήσῃ·
paragraphs.translit: isthi eunoōn tō antidikō sou tachy heōs hotou ei metʼ autou en tē hodō, mēpote se paradō ho antidikos tō kritē, kai ho kritēs tō hypēretē, kai eis phylakēn blēthēsē·

paragraphs.text: Verily I say unto thee, thou shalt by no means come out thence, till thou have paid the last farthing.
paragraphs.original: ἀμὴν λέγω σοι, οὐ μὴ ἐξέλθῃς ἐκεῖθεν ἕως ἂν ἀποδῷς τὸν ἔσχατον κοδράντην.
paragraphs.translit: amēn legō soi, ou mē exelthēs ekeithen heōs an apodōs ton eschaton kodrantēn.

paragraphs.text: Ye have heard that it was said, Thou shalt not commit adultery:
paragraphs.original: Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη· Οὐ μοιχεύσεις.
paragraphs.translit: Ēkousate hoti errethē· Ou moicheuseis.

paragraphs.text: but I say unto you, that every one that looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.
paragraphs.original: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ βλέπων γυναῖκα πρὸς τὸ ἐπιθυμῆσαι αὐτὴν ἤδη ἐμοίχευσεν αὐτὴν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: egō de legō hymin hoti pas ho blepōn gynaika pros to epithymēsai autēn ēdē emoicheusen autēn en tē kardia autou.

paragraphs.text: And if thy right eye causeth thee to stumble, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not thy whole body be cast into hell.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ὁ δεξιὸς σκανδαλίζει σε, ἔξελε αὐτὸν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ, συμφέρει γάρ σοι ἵνα ἀπόληται ἓν τῶν μελῶν σου καὶ μὴ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου βληθῇ εἰς γέενναν.
paragraphs.translit: ei de ho ophthalmos sou ho dexios skandalizei se, exele auton kai bale apo sou, sympherei gar soi hina apolētai hen tōn melōn sou kai mē holon to sōma sou blēthē eis geennan.

paragraphs.text: And if thy right hand causeth thee to stumble, cut it off, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not thy whole body go into hell.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἰ ἡ δεξιά σου χεὶρ σκανδαλίζει σε, ἔκκοψον αὐτὴν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ, συμφέρει γάρ σοι ἵνα ἀπόληται ἓν τῶν μελῶν σου καὶ μὴ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου εἰς γέενναν ἀπέλθῃ.
paragraphs.translit: kai ei hē dexia sou cheir skandalizei se, ekkopson autēn kai bale apo sou, sympherei gar soi hina apolētai hen tōn melōn sou kai mē holon to sōma sou eis geennan apelthē.

paragraphs.text: It was said also, Whosoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorcement:
paragraphs.original: Ἐρρέθη δέ· Ὃς ἂν ἀπολύσῃ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ, δότω αὐτῇ ἀποστάσιον.
paragraphs.translit: Errethē de· Hos an apolysē tēn gynaika autou, dotō autē apostasion.

paragraphs.text: but I say unto you, that every one that putteth away his wife, saving for the cause of fornication, maketh her an adulteress: and whosoever shall marry her when she is put away committeth adultery.
paragraphs.original: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ἀπολύων τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ παρεκτὸς λόγου πορνείας ποιεῖ αὐτὴν μοιχευθῆναι, καὶ ὃς ἐὰν ἀπολελυμένην γαμήσῃ μοιχᾶται.
paragraphs.translit: egō de legō hymin hoti pas ho apolyōn tēn gynaika autou parektos logou porneias poiei autēn moicheuthēnai, kai hos ean apolelymenēn gamēsē moichatai.

paragraphs.text: Again, ye have heard that it was said to them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto the Lord thine oaths:
paragraphs.original: Πάλιν ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη τοῖς ἀρχαίοις· Οὐκ ἐπιορκήσεις, ἀποδώσεις δὲ τῷ κυρίῳ τοὺς ὅρκους σου.
paragraphs.translit: Palin ēkousate hoti errethē tois archaiois· Ouk epiorkēseis, apodōseis de tō kyriō tous horkous sou.

paragraphs.text: but I say unto you, swear not at all; neither by the heaven, for it is the throne of God;
paragraphs.original: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν μὴ ὀμόσαι ὅλως· μήτε ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, ὅτι θρόνος ἐστὶν τοῦ θεοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: egō de legō hymin mē omosai holōs· mēte en tō ouranō, hoti thronos estin tou theou·

paragraphs.text: nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet; nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
paragraphs.original: μήτε ἐν τῇ γῇ, ὅτι ὑποπόδιόν ἐστιν τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ· μήτε εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, ὅτι πόλις ἐστὶν τοῦ μεγάλου βασιλέως·
paragraphs.translit: mēte en tē gē, hoti hypopodion estin tōn podōn autou· mēte eis Hierosolyma, hoti polis estin tou megalou basileōs·

paragraphs.text: Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, for thou canst not make one hair white or black.
paragraphs.original: μήτε ἐν τῇ κεφαλῇ σου ὀμόσῃς, ὅτι οὐ δύνασαι μίαν τρίχα λευκὴν ποιῆσαι ἢ μέλαιναν.
paragraphs.translit: mēte en tē kephalē sou omosēs, hoti ou dynasai mian tricha leukēn poiēsai ē melainan.

paragraphs.text: But let your speech be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: and whatsoever is more than these is of the evil [one].
paragraphs.original: ἔστω δὲ ὁ λόγος ὑμῶν ναὶ ναί, οὒ οὔ· τὸ δὲ περισσὸν τούτων ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: estō de ho logos hymōn nai nai, ou ou· to de perisson toutōn ek tou ponērou estin.

paragraphs.text: Ye have heard that it was said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth:
paragraphs.original: Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη· Ὀφθαλμὸν ἀντὶ ὀφθαλμοῦ καὶ ὀδόντα ἀντὶ ὀδόντος.
paragraphs.translit: Ēkousate hoti errethē· Ophthalmon anti ophthalmou kai odonta anti odontos.

paragraphs.text: but I say unto you, resist not him that is evil: but whosoever smiteth thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.
paragraphs.original: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν μὴ ἀντιστῆναι τῷ πονηρῷ· ἀλλʼ ὅστις σε ῥαπίζει εἰς τὴν δεξιὰν σιαγόνα, στρέψον αὐτῷ καὶ τὴν ἄλλην·
paragraphs.translit: egō de legō hymin mē antistēnai tō ponērō· allʼ hostis se rhapizei eis tēn dexian siagona, strepson autō kai tēn allēn·

paragraphs.text: And if any man would go to law with thee, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloak also.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τῷ θέλοντί σοι κριθῆναι καὶ τὸν χιτῶνά σου λαβεῖν, ἄφες αὐτῷ καὶ τὸ ἱμάτιον·
paragraphs.translit: kai tō thelonti soi krithēnai kai ton chitōna sou labein, aphes autō kai to himation·

paragraphs.text: And whosoever shall compel thee to go one mile, go with him two.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὅστις σε ἀγγαρεύσει μίλιον ἕν, ὕπαγε μετʼ αὐτοῦ δύο.
paragraphs.translit: kai hostis se angareusei milion hen, hypage metʼ autou dyo.

paragraphs.text: Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away.
paragraphs.original: τῷ αἰτοῦντί σε δός, καὶ τὸν θέλοντα ἀπὸ σοῦ δανίσασθαι μὴ ἀποστραφῇς.
paragraphs.translit: tō aitounti se dos, kai ton thelonta apo sou danisasthai mē apostraphēs.

paragraphs.text: Ye have heard that it was said, Thou shalt love thy neighbor, and hate thine enemy:
paragraphs.original: Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη· Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου καὶ μισήσεις τὸν ἐχθρόν σου.
paragraphs.translit: Ēkousate hoti errethē· Agapēseis ton plēsion sou kai misēseis ton echthron sou.

paragraphs.text: but I say unto you, love your enemies, and pray for them that persecute you;
paragraphs.original: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑμῶν καὶ προσεύχεσθε ὑπὲρ τῶν διωκόντων ὑμᾶς·
paragraphs.translit: egō de legō hymin, agapate tous echthrous hymōn kai proseuchesthe hyper tōn diōkontōn hymas·

paragraphs.text: that ye may be sons of your Father who is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sendeth rain on the just and the unjust.
paragraphs.original: ὅπως γένησθε υἱοὶ τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς, ὅτι τὸν ἥλιον αὐτοῦ ἀνατέλλει ἐπὶ πονηροὺς καὶ ἀγαθοὺς καὶ βρέχει ἐπὶ δικαίους καὶ ἀδίκους.
paragraphs.translit: hopōs genēsthe hyioi tou patros hymōn tou en ouranois, hoti ton hēlion autou anatellei epi ponērous kai agathous kai brechei epi dikaious kai adikous.

paragraphs.text: For if ye love them that love you, what reward have ye? do not even the publicans the same?
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν γὰρ ἀγαπήσητε τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας ὑμᾶς, τίνα μισθὸν ἔχετε; οὐχὶ καὶ οἱ τελῶναι τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν;
paragraphs.translit: ean gar agapēsēte tous agapōntas hymas, tina misthon echete; ouchi kai hoi telōnai to auto poiousin;

paragraphs.text: And if ye salute your brethren only, what do ye more [than others?] do not even the Gentiles the same?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐὰν ἀσπάσησθε τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ὑμῶν μόνον, τί περισσὸν ποιεῖτε; οὐχὶ καὶ οἱ ἐθνικοὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν;
paragraphs.translit: kai ean aspasēsthe tous adelphous hymōn monon, ti perisson poieite; ouchi kai hoi ethnikoi to auto poiousin;

paragraphs.text: Ye therefore shall be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.
paragraphs.original: Ἔσεσθε οὖν ὑμεῖς τέλειοι ὡς ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος τέλειός ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: Esesthe oun hymeis teleioi hōs ho patēr hymōn ho ouranios teleios estin.
